solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Officer back with tea

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it
mate is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: A police officer returns carrying a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as 'returning' but is the verb meaning support, as in seconding a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: On a merchant ship the second mate is a deck officer ranking below the first mate.

clue.text: Concessions for high voices?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: small things given to placate someone

definitions.note: the question mark flags an abbreviation: sopranos shortened
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a casual short form for sopranos

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests singers being given special treatment; the question mark warns that the second meaning is a clipped informal word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a placatory offering, and sop is also a shortened form of soprano, the highest singing part.

clue.text: Caterpillar maybe avoiding hill, climbs barrow

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, turning the letters back to front
to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so those letters are left out

parts.note: Caterpillar is a maker of tractors, so it is an example of one
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A caterpillar crawling up a wheelbarrow while steering clear of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caterpillar' looks like the insect but is the machinery brand, standing for a tractor by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is a small hand-pushed cart, so the two words are close synonyms for a wheeled carrier.

clue.text: Pristine toy soldiers, participants in civil war

parts.note: pristine means unused, fresh
a collection of toy soldiers is a model army

explanation.surface: A mint-condition set of toy soldiers reenacting the English Civil War.
explanation.walkthrough: The toy soldiers seem to be the thing described, but they supply the second part of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Model Army was the Parliamentarian force formed in 1645 that fought the Royalists in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Chewy artist?

parts.note: surface reading: a painter whose work is tough or chewy
setter's reading: a painter whose surname is itself a verb for chewing

explanation.walkthrough: Edvard Munch, the Norwegian painter of The Scream, has a surname that means to chew noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian expressionist painter's surname is also an everyday word for chewing food steadily.

clue.text: Well done: in a daze, showing patience

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a daze is a trance, the article included in the phrase
olé is a cheer of approval, as at a bullfight

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who stayed patient while half dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' looks like the verdict on a steak or a job, but it is the Spanish cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the capacity to put up with things calmly, the same quality as patience.

clue.text: Friend attending Mass this Sunday?

definitions.note: the answer names which Sunday, so it fills the gap before the word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
M is the scientific symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A friend comes along to church for Mass on a particular Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' seems to be the church service, but it is the physics symbol. The question mark shows the definition is completed by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm Sunday, the Sunday before Easter, commemorates Jesus entering Jerusalem to crowds waving branches.

clue.text: A chap has troublesome issue about new copyist

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means around, so one set of letters goes round another
something troublesome is disordered and unruly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a chap is a man
the letters to be jumbled
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A man with a problematic matter concerning a new copyist he has hired.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled five letters go round N, after A and a man; 'about' reads as 'concerning' but means around.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is someone employed to write from dictation or copy manuscripts, a literary assistant or scribe.

clue.text: Three-card trick on film is capital

parts.note: three-card monte is the street con of finding the lady
a film can be a video recording

explanation.surface: A film showing a card-sharp trick is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as the old British word for excellent, but it is a noun: a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Montevideo is the capital city of Uruguay, on the estuary of the River Plate.

clue.text: I get out with difficulty after salesman turns blue

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed second, so the order in the answer is the reverse of the clue's
turning round makes the letters face the other way

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
taken as written
to winkle out is to extract something with effort

explanation.surface: Someone struggles free once a salesman goes blue in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns blue' looks like one phrase, but 'turns' belongs to the salesman and 'blue' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Periwinkle is a soft lavender-blue shade named after the flower of the periwinkle plant.

clue.text: One in front resembling a peacock

indicators.note: something in another is held inside it

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The bird at the head of the line looks like a peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: Van as the leading part comes from vanguard, the front of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacocks strut and display their plumage, so they are proverbial for vanity and conceited pride.

clue.text: I might be hearing "icicle", apparently

parts.note: surface reading: someone listening in on a conversation
setter's reading: an icicle literally drops from the edge of a roof

explanation.walkthrough: An icicle hangs and drips from the overhang of a roof, so it is literally something dropping from there; the listener sense is the real meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who secretly listens to private talk is so named from standing under the roof overhang to overhear.

clue.text: Universal Earth mentor? Fantastic!

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and far-fetched, so the letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
the rest of the letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a guide for the whole planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and description: the personified force of nature is a teacher to all the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother Nature personifies the natural world as a nurturing figure who guides and teaches all living things.

clue.text: Restrain part of hand that is a bit redundant

parts.note: to check is to hold back
a digit is a finger

explanation.surface: Holding back a finger that has become surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' reads as 'somewhat', but it points to a single character in a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A check digit is an extra character added to a code, carrying no new information, used only to detect errors.

clue.text: One walking along composing porn? Dear me!

indicators.note: composing means putting together in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shocked reaction to a passer-by writing smut.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to picture a stroller writing smut; the phrase 'Dear me' is not an exclamation but six letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenader strolls along a seafront or public walk, taking a leisurely walk for pleasure.

clue.text: Buffoon, one of several appearing together on short London street

indicators.note: something cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: Harley Street, the London street known for private doctors, with its end removed
a quin is one of five babies born at one birth

explanation.surface: A clown who is one of a troupe performing on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The quin is placed on (after) the shortened street name; Harley Street is famous in London for its medical practices.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the comic servant of the Italian commedia dell'arte and pantomime, a clowning figure in diamond costume.

clue.text: Exiled without husband after old city became more industrial

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to be exiled is to be banished
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Sent away without her husband after the old city became a factory town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur is the crossword's favourite old city. The wordplay's piece is placed after it, as 'after' instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: A region that is urbanised has taken on towns, factories and city development, growing more built-up.

clue.text: Tedium something of an unspoken nuisance

indicators.note: something of a thing is just a portion of it, so a run of letters is taken from inside

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Boredom as a quiet, unspoken irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of 'unspoken' and the start of 'nuisance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French borrowing for listless weariness and boredom, the same state as tedium.

clue.text: Mike in unresponsive state? Just a short break

indicators.note: one thing in another is held inside it

parts.note: a coma is a state of unconsciousness
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Mike lies unconscious; perhaps it is only a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a person, but it is the radio code word for the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma marks the briefest pause in a sentence, the shortest break in punctuation.

clue.text: Wait here for food, money and some coke, possibly

definitions.note: a phrase describing a place, standing for the noun

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a line is a portion of cocaine laid out to be snorted

explanation.surface: Instructions to hang around for food, cash and perhaps a drink or drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food, money' look like a list, but food belongs to the definition and money alone gives the first piece; 'possibly' marks the line as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadline is a queue of poor people waiting to receive free food from charity.

clue.text: Withdrawing name for a post in religious organisation?

parts.note: de- is a prefix of removal or reversal, as in de-select
a nomination puts a name forward for a position

explanation.surface: Taking back a candidate's name for a job in a church body.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as de-nomination: taking away a nomination, which is how the setter frames withdrawing a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A denomination is a distinct branch of a religion, such as Methodism or the Baptist church.

clue.text: Article missing its last odd loose thread

indicators.note: missing the final letter means the end is cut off

parts.note: the is the definite article
rum is British slang for strange

explanation.surface: A garment is lacking its final odd loose end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like an item of clothing but is the grammar word. Rum meaning odd is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In weaving, a thrum is the fringe of unwoven warp threads left on the loom, a loose end of yarn.

clue.text: In good condition to cover area in short order

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it

parts.note: fit means healthy, in good shape
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Keeping an area in good repair, done promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short order' looks like the phrase for quickly; the definition is just the last two words, meaning a brief command.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree, a command issued by someone with power, often summarily.

clue.text: Woman's death overcoming one

indicators.note: to overcome is to come over, so one piece covers another

parts.note: death is one's end
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman's death defeating a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is not possessive: it stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a woman's given name, as in Enid Blyton, so it serves as an example of a woman.

clue.text: Judge of the Bible not available for foreign author

indicators.note: not means leaving something out, so letters are removed

parts.note: Gideon was one of the judges of Israel in the Book of Judges
on can mean available, as in 'on tap'

explanation.surface: A biblical judge who cannot be reached to rule on a foreign writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The judge's name loses its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: André Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate, so for British solvers he is a foreign writer.

clue.text: A share certificate, not one arranged for credit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: arranged means put in order afresh, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: scrip is a certificate of a share holding
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A share certificate that was not issued in exchange for credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one' reads as a denial, but both words are letters for the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascription is the act of attributing something to a cause or person, so it means giving credit.

clue.text: Seabird's opportunity to be heard

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: your turn is your opportunity to act

explanation.surface: A seabird gets its chance to make itself heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s stands for 'is', linking the bird to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns are slender, fork-tailed seabirds related to gulls, found along coasts worldwide.

clue.text: Vaguely indicated a beat: cued at last, drum messed up

indicators.note: messing something up throws it into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word just before

parts.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drummer sketchily marked the rhythm, then botched the cue at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical scene hides a plain jumble of the letters plus the last one of 'cued'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to outline or foreshadow something faintly, giving only a shadowy sketch of it.
